questions.subject: EUROPEAN_HISTORY
questions.stem: For a military memo, identify Peter the Great's key military innovation.

options.text: He created a standing army and navy based on European models.
He abolished the army to fund culture only.
He rejected all European military techniques.
He armed only peasants and excluded nobles.

questions.explanation: Peter built European-style army and navy. Abolition or rejection misstate reforms.

questions.subject: EUROPEAN_HISTORY
questions.stem: In a city planner's memo for a religious conflict exhibit, explain the religious dimension of the English Civil War.

answer.exemplar: Tensions between Anglican royalists, Puritan parliamentarians, and fears of Catholic absolutism intertwined with constitutional disputes to fuel war.

questions.explanation: Religion and constitution intertwined. The wrong view sees purely economic motives, understating religion.

questions.subject: EUROPEAN_HISTORY
questions.stem: While drafting a memo for a legacy exhibit, synthesize the long-term impact of the Glorious Revolution.

options.text: It had no lasting effect on English governance.
It restored absolute monarchy permanently.
It established constitutional monarchy and parliamentary supremacy.
It abolished Parliament in favor of royal rule.

questions.explanation: 1688 created constitutional monarchy. No effect or absolutism misstate legacy.

questions.subject: EUROPEAN_HISTORY
questions.learningObjective: Analyzes a source about resistance theory

stimulus.body: Resistance to tyrants is obedience to God. When a king breaks the fundamental law, subjects may defend their rights. Royal authority is conditional on justice.

questions.stem: A city planner's memo review of a resistance theory panel asks what the source best supports.

options.text: Kings may never be resisted under any circumstances.
Subjects owe no duties to any government.
Royal authority is absolute and unconditional.
Resistance to unjust rulers can be justified.

questions.explanation: The source justifies resistance to tyranny. Absolute obedience or unconditional authority misread it.

questions.subject: EUROPEAN_HISTORY
questions.stem: While drafting a memo for a government purpose exhibit, synthesize Locke's view of government's role.

options.text: Government exists to protect natural rights through consent.
Government exists to maximize royal power and glory.
Government should abolish all private property.
Government has no purpose beyond military conquest.

questions.explanation: Locke limited government to rights protection. Royal power or conquest misstate his view.

questions.subject: EUROPEAN_HISTORY
questions.learningObjective: Identifies Hobbes's view of human nature
questions.stem: For a human nature memo, identify Hobbes's view of humans in the state of nature.

options.text: Humans are naturally cooperative and peaceful without government.
Humans are naturally divine and sinless.
Humans are self-interested and prone to conflict without sovereign.
Humans require no government because they are rational angels.

questions.explanation: Hobbes saw humans as self-interested and conflict-prone. Cooperative or angelic views misstate his theory.

questions.subject: EUROPEAN_HISTORY
questions.stem: In a city planner's memo for a judicial district, explain why judicial independence matters in separation of powers.

answer.exemplar: Independent judges apply law impartially without executive or legislative pressure, protecting rights and preventing arbitrary power.

questions.explanation: Judicial independence ensures impartial law. The wrong view merges courts with executive, undermining protection.

questions.subject: EUROPEAN_HISTORY
questions.learningObjective: Analyzes a source about Voltaire's deism

stimulus.body: Voltaire argued for a creator God and natural religion, rejecting atheism and clerical dogma alike. He saw tolerance as essential to civil peace.

questions.stem: A city planner's memo review of a religious thought panel asks what the source best supports.

options.text: Voltaire was a militant atheist who rejected all religion.
He believed religion should be enforced by violence.
He endorsed clerical control of the state.
He supported deism and toleration while rejecting dogma.

questions.explanation: The source supports deism and toleration. Atheism or clerical control misread it.

questions.subject: EUROPEAN_HISTORY
questions.stem: For a legacy memo, evaluate Rousseau's influence on later democratic thought.

options.text: Rousseau's general will inspired both democratic and authoritarian readings.
Rousseau had no influence on any later political movement.
His ideas were used only by absolute monarchs.
He directly caused all modern democracies without controversy.

questions.explanation: Rousseau influenced both democratic and authoritarian thought. No influence or only monarchs misstate legacy.
